title.narrative: Lifesaving Protection, WASH, Health and Nutrition Assistance to Displacement and Famine in River Nile

description.narrative: ltpgtRiver Nile state holds 11% of the IDP caseload across Sudan. The influx of displaced people in RN state is straining food security and nutrition, especially for vulnerable groups, such as children. Food is available but not affordable for the majority of IDPs. The surge in population has stretched local WASH systems, threatening the health of both residents and displaced people. Against this backdrop, Save the Children (SC) in partnership with Nada Elazhar for Disaster Prevention and Sustainable Development (NADA) aim to support the most vulnerable children and families to meet basic needs and reduce high morbidity, acute malnutrition, disease outbreaks and exposure to protection risks by increasing access to integrated, disability-inclusive and gender-sensitive health, nutrition, WASH, and protection services in Atbara Locality. To achieve this, under the leadership of Save the Children (SC), the Consortium will contribute to improving equitable and inclusive access to quality life-saving curative and preventative healthcare services through two health facilities (Alnahda and Alwhuda HFs), in Atbara, covering prioritized locations with the most vulnerable populations in the target district. To fill identified health and nutrition gaps including medical supplies, incentives, minor rehabilitations and referrals and increase the coverage, the project will target women of reproductive age, with a focus on pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5 years of age, while providing gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive lifesaving healthcare for communicable and non-communicable diseases among children over 5, adults and the elderly. The proposed health interventions will provide essential maternal and child health services, essential medication, and supplies (PPE, diagnostics, case management), establish referral pathways and strengthen the immunization services. lt/pgtltpgtLikewise, SC will provide emergency lifesaving nutrition services with an emphasis on increasing access for 4,504 conflict-affected people in Atbara, including community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and preventive nutrition services. The project will be securing nutrition supplies, contributing to facilities running cost, and establishing linkages between stabilisation centres, OTP and TSFP sites. Emphasis will also be given to preventive nutrition services of IYCF community-based support of IYCF through mother support groups, and IYCF in exceptionally difficult circumstances (IYCF-E) with focus on one-to-one IYCF counselling and support for mothers, promotion of breastfeeding and hygienelt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo reduce morbidity and mortality associated with water-related disease outbreaks and environmental health risks, SC and NADA will also improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene knowledge for approximately 26,000 individuals. The Consortium will ensure that the two targeted health facilities are equipped with necessary WASH infrastructure and materials, including water purification systems, excreta disposal facilities, cleaning materials, and solid waste management systems. We will also ensure that targeted communities have access to safe WASH services including access to safe water, sanitation, proper waste management and hygiene promotion.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtLastly, under the leadership of NADA, the Consortium will provide an integrated GBV, CP and GP response to conflict-affected communities, including children, women and people with disabilities. The project will conduct regular protection monitoring. CBPNs members and active community members will be trained and actively engaged in the protection monitoring. NADA will provide mental health and psychosocial support services including provision of psychological first aid, social and life skills interventions and recreational for GBV Survivors, elderly, female head household, elderly. The project will also train service providers on, in particular, legal, health and social care providers on PSEA. ltbrgt ltbrgt lt/pgt
